caption: I m turning 23, I feel doomed to never be chosen, and I am suicidal. Three times, I have become involved with women who never truly chose me. In each case, I was kept secret, compared to other women and made to feel inadequate. They said they were not ready for a relationship, but eventually left me or cheated and then became official with someone else. Suddenly, they were willing to post pictures, go on dates and publicly offer another woman everything they had refused me. After seeing this happen repeatedly, it is becoming difficult not to interpret it as evidence that something is fundamentally wrong with me. I have not remained passive. I have gone to therapy, read books such as Women Who Love Too Much and Attached , and worked seriously on attachment, boundaries, self worth and my attraction to unavailable people. The first time, I abandoned myself completely. I tolerated uncertainty, inconsistency and mistreatment because I was desperate to preserve the connection. The second time happened just as I was beginning to recover. She love bombed me and, within two weeks, told me she wanted a relationship. Then she changed her mind. I tried to leave, but she persuaded me to remain in an undefined situation where she retained emotional and romantic access to me without committing. I recognised the pattern sooner, but it still felt like being knocked down in exactly the same place. The third time seemed different. There was no love bombing, and things appeared to be progressing naturally. Then she told me she was going through a complicated period, did not know whether she could be a good partner and was unsure she was capable of a relationship. This time, I ended it. I did what I had supposedly learned to do I believed her, protected myself and refused another ambiguous situation. Within weeks, however, she was back with her ex girlfriend, posting pictures everywhere. Once again, someone who had told me she could not be a partner suddenly became perfectly capable of being one with somebody else. That public element is perhaps the most painful part. I am told the problem is timing or emotional unavailability, only to watch that unavailability disappear almost immediately for another woman. Most of my friends seem to enter relationships naturally. Meanwhile, ordinary things proper dates, photographs together, travelling, meeting friends, being introduced as someone s girlfriend have begun to feel like impossible fantasies. I know rationally that I am not unattractive or unlovable. I have friends and family who care about me. But emotionally, I feel cursed, because I no longer know how else to understand the same experience happening repeatedly. Being a lesbian intensifies the hopelessness. It is already difficult to meet women who are available, compatible and interested in commitment. When I change my dating app preferences to men, I immediately receive hundreds of likes. I know this is not necessarily meaningful, but the contrast makes dating women feel even scarcer. I am turning 23 in a few days. I know that is young, but the accumulation of these experiences has left me profoundly hopeless and isolated. I have been experiencing suicidal thoughts every day. Sometimes the pain feels so unbearable that I fear this may be my last birthday. I am posting because I need help understanding this pattern and stopping myself from seeing it as proof that I will never be chosen.

caption: hopeless and this is my situation. 32F I grew up in a family where we never really talked about our inner lives or the details of our daily experiences. Conversations were always about whatever was right in front of us whether we should eat more, whether the food tasted good, whether we were tired. Everything revolved around money and status. My father was the unquestioned authority in the family, and I grew up with an emotional absence of fatherly love. My mother was always the one who endured and suppressed her feelings. Although my parents never argued in front of us, they also never showed affection toward each other. After graduating from university and throughout my twenties, I met many different people and had many social circles. Looking back, those relationships only existed within group settings. No one would text me unless it was a guy who was romantically interested in me. I genuinely believed nothing was wrong with that. I thought we were all close friends, but in reality they were just drinking buddies or activity companions. I thought I was sincere, but I have since realised that I have always been a passive participant in relationships. When I was with a group of people, no one noticed anything unusual because I simply responded to whatever everyone else was talking about. Looking back, I was almost never the person who initiated conversations or introduced new ideas. Instead, someone else would share an interest, and only then would I go and learn about it. For example, if a friend wanted to go skiing, I would enjoy skiing with them not because I was personally interested in skiing, but because they were. Once I left that group, I completely lost interest in those activities and never looked them up or pursued them on my own. For years, I treated work as something to endure while waiting for the weekend. I thought that was normal. In reality, I was using weekends and social activities to escape from work instead of building a meaningful life of my own. In romantic relationships, I struggled to let go because I believed the other person was a good person, but I was also using the relationship to avoid facing my own inner emptiness and the fear of being alone. Looking back, I realise I was constantly avoiding myself. I resisted growing up because I always assumed someone would catch me if I fell. I believed that, if everything went wrong, I could simply leave Australia and return home. Many basic aspects of daily life never seemed important to me because I assumed my mother or our domestic helper would always take care of them. I knew these responsibilities existed, but I severely underestimated how difficult it would be to live independently. At the time, my understanding of life was simply too limited. I never thought about how difficult it becomes to make genuine friends in your thirties, or how much convenience and lifestyle differences matter. I wanted many things in life, but I never fought wholeheartedly for them. I also failed to realise how much time changes relationships, and I never confronted the fact that I had never built deep, genuine connections with people. Perhaps people also sensed that I wasn t someone who sought deep friendships. More importantly, they probably saw me as a hollow person. I never really shared my own life because, in truth, there wasn t much to share. My life consisted only of going to work, coming home, and spending time with other people. TBC

caption: Well Defined Outcome. Why "I want to be more confident" never actually happens Vague goals give your brain nothing to act on. "Stop being anxious in meetings" "Speak up once per meeting." 2 Make it about your own actions only not what other people should do. Add context when, where, with whom does this apply? You might want more assertiveness at work, not with your partner in bed. 3 Break it into the next physical step. Not "write a book," but "write one page today." 4 Set a check in date to review what's working. Example "I want to be more confident" becomes "By Friday, I'll start one conversation a day with someone new at work, and I'll check in on how it felt each night." That's testable. "Be more confident" isn't. Try rewriting one goal you have right now using steps 1 4. You'll feel the difference immediately.

caption: Has anyone overcome work anxiety with positive self talk?. I'm currently in the process of being assessed for ADHD, and one thing that's become increasingly clear to me is how much my ADHD traits seem to fuel my anxiety in various ways. For me, things like overthinking, worrying about saying the wrong thing, coming across the way i.e. rude from interrupting people, and constantly second guessing myself all seem to feed into my anxiety. It's caused me problems for years. I get incredibly anxious before social situations, even though, once I'm actually there, they're usually nowhere near as bad as I'd imagined. After five or ten minutes, I tend to settle down, but the anticipation beforehand can be absolutely awful. I ve had a couple of panic attacks in the past. But the real problem is work. I work for an agency, so I'm regularly introduced to new clients. Even though I'm experienced, know my job well, and I'm always well prepared, I still become incredibly anxious beforehand to the point where I've had panic attacks. If a meeting is scheduled for later in the day, I often can't focus on anything else. I spend hours worrying about it instead of getting my work done because my mind is completely consumed by the meeting. Then, when the call starts, my brain just seems to freeze. I struggle to think of what to say, I stutter, stumble over my words, take ages to answer questions, and end up waffling because I'm so nervous. It's especially embarrassing if one of my colleagues is on the call as well, because I feel like they're seeing me at my worst. Afterwards, I replay everything in my head and beat myself up over every little mistake. I end up calling myself an idiot and convincing myself I've made a terrible impression. It becomes a vicious cycle, because all of that just makes me even more anxious about the next meeting. Now I don t want to work in a job or career that makes me feel this way. Life is too short. BUT frustrating part is that I don't want to change jobs because of this. For the most part, I really enjoy what I do. I've made some great friends at work, we have a good laugh, the company is pretty laid back compared to a lot of others, and I'm good at my job. The irony is that this is really the only part of my job I don't feel confident in. Writing, strategy, and the actual work itself don't bother me. It's the client facing side of things meeting new people, pitching ideas, selling myself, and thinking on the spot that completely throws me. I know that if I could get this anxiety under control, I'd probably be a lot better at that side of my job. caption: Please any advice is appreciated. Hi, I'm an 18 year old girl, an only child, and I ve always had a pretty complicated relationship with my parents. For a while now, I ve been feeling a strong turmoil inside. I m seeing a psychiatrist because until recently I suffered from depression and social anxiety, and I still have a lot of anxiety related to school. During a session, my psychiatrist told me that he thinks my parents are overly controlling and that, as soon as I have the chance to be independent, I should take it. From that moment on, I started wondering what kind of people my parents really are. As a child, I didn't realize a lot of things. I d get slapped for what were just simple "tantrums" for a child I was threatened with more slaps if I did certain things, and over time, I learned to cry silently because I knew that if my dad heard me, he would get even angrier. My mom always told me not to tell the teachers or other kids anything. When you're little, it's normal to trust your parents and do what they say. Now, though, looking back, I realize that many of their behaviors were anything but normal. Even when I went to the psychologist and the social worker for the first time, my mom repeated to me not to say anything about my dad's behaviors. Especially my dad, when I was younger, would slap me, but he stopped as I grew up. The problem is he suffers from strong moments of anger and depressive periods during which he openly says, both to me and my mom, that he wants to end it all... For example, due to a fight with our neighbors, who were also relatives, we were forced to move. To this day, he deeply hates them. In those moments of anger, he doesn t talk to anyone or, when he does, it s almost always to insult someone. Lately, this happens more often because we have financial problems my mom is a housewife and my dad works as a garden plant grower. All of my dad's relatives always told my mom that he "is just like that" and that, sooner or later, it will pass. And indeed, after a while, he acts like nothing happened. I want to clarify one thing he has never raised his hands against my mom, even though he does throw some insults her way. Most of the insults are directed at me, at what I do or how I behave. I often feel like I m the outlet for his anger. I ve tried several times to talk to my mom. I reminded her that when I was little, she said not to tell certain things because otherwise, they would take me away from her. However, she insists she never said anything like that and claims that these are memories I made up. She keeps telling me that my dad is just like this, that she has always put up with it, and that I should too because, after all, he loves me. And that s exactly the point. I know that my dad loves me. When he s not angry, he jokes with me, talks to me, and acts like a caring father. That s also why I ve never told anyone anything. I keep wondering if I m exaggerating, if maybe the problem is me, or if I m misinterpreting what s happening. Even while writing this post, I feel conflicted. Today, for instance, he got mad because I don t go out enough, because I often stay in bed or on the couch with my phone. The subjects of his insults are always the same, but they hurt every time. I ve never had a big group of friends. I ve always had one or two people close by, who often disappeared just when I needed them. I have low self esteem, probably also due to my relationship with my dad and the bullying I suffered in elementary school, where I was excluded or made fun of. Do you know what hurt me the most? My dad sided with the bullies. He would say those weren t real problems, that they were just kids jokes, and that I was too whiny. Now, though, he gets upset because I m always home alone with my phone. And the worst part is that I can t even try to respond to him because in his house he must always be right. Of course, my mom always finds an excuse for his behaviors. She says he does it for my own good, that they were both only children, and that they don t want to see me living an isolated life. It s one of the many speeches I hear repeated endlessly. The other is "We love you, we ve never made you lack anything." It s true that, sometimes, they spend money on me, but almost exclusively for things considered useful. For example, they bought me an iPad for studying, but my dad told me flat out "If I see you using it to play or for anything that isn t studying, trust me, you ll see me really angry." They ve also paid for driving school but accompanied it with phrases like "If you fail, you ll pay for your license with your own money. You ve got more than I do," referring to the money my grandma gave me for my future when I turned eighteen. And it doesn t end there. They are also very controlling. caption: Psychology assumed that helping others feel better was a universal human motive. A study of 6,900 people just showed it is not. When someone you care about is upset, the impulse feels automatic. You reach toward them, you say something reassuring, you try to shift the mood. If you grew up in the United States, Germany, or the United Kingdom, this response probably feels not just natural but morally obvious. Leaving someone to sit in their pain without trying to alleviate it can feel like a failure of empathy, a withdrawal of care. The entire edifice of Western therapy is built on this premise negative emotions are problems, and helping someone feel better is the goal. A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences has tested that premise across 17 countries and more than 6,900 people. What it found is that the impulse to eliminate another person s distress is not a human universal. It is a cultural product, specific to societies that organize themselves around individual happiness and personal achievement. In collectivistic cultures, which account for the majority of the world s population, negative emotions are not problems to be solved. They are tools to be used, and the most caring thing a person can do is often to leave them intact.

caption: Sex Is Good For You, Actually In 1990, 55 percent of American adults between 18 and 64 had sex at least once a week. In 2024, that number dropped to 37 percent. What is happening? Unpaywalled. Even our Neanderthal predecessors felt the perks Sex helped them build strong connections and collaborate with partners. In contemporary times, though, sex simply doesn t seem to have the same panache. And the signs of our apathy towards it have been bubbling for a while. In a 2012 poll conducted by the Today Show and dating site Match.com , 32 percent of single people said they d rather give up sex for a year than their favorite food. Surprisingly, individuals in relationships didn t feel much differently 28 percent preferred chow over a romp. Fast forward to 2026, an EduBirdie poll showing 67 percent of Gen Z prefer a good night of sleep over sex doesn t look too shocking. It s unlikely that sex itself has somehow become less enjoyable than things like sleep, and much more likely that the cognitive tradeoffs have changed. Sex is wound up in the ever expanding attention economy, jockeying for position with the bevy of other energy depleting or preserving things, like social media, outings with friends, and, yes, sleep. One study hypothesized that the iPhone s introduction in 2007 contributed to 33 percent to 52 percent of the dip in general fertility rate among women between 15 and 44 years old. But why? Our digital immersion and embrace of parasocialism, largely one sided intimacy with celebrities and influencers, means we can accrue the benefits of social connection on demand and without the upfront infusion of effort usually required to find and sustain sexual relationships. caption: New research suggests the brain doesn't switch cleanly between being awake and asleep it can produce dream like experiences before you're fully asleep.. A recent study used EEG recordings to examine what people experience during the transition from wakefulness to sleep. Participants were repeatedly awakened during that period and asked what had been going through their minds just before the alarm. One of the more interesting findings was that dream like imagery wasn't limited to sleep. Some participants reported vivid, bizarre experiences while their brain activity still showed signs of wakefulness, while others in light sleep were simply thinking about ordinary things like work or plans for tomorrow. Rather than a simple "awake logical thinking" and "asleep dreaming" model, the researchers suggest that the transition is much more gradual, with different mental states overlapping before we fully fall asleep. It made me think about those moments where you're lying in bed and suddenly realize your thoughts have turned into something that barely makes sense almost like dreaming before you're actually asleep.

caption: My best friend s boyfriend says I should be stoned to death. My best friend wants me to meet her boyfriend but he thinks I deserve to die. I 39M have been best friends with my 38F friend for about 24 years. Her parents are basically my second set of parents. A few months ago, she met her boyfriend 29M on TikTok. They started a long distance relationship with back and forth visits she flew up to him some weekends, he flew down to her others. After a few months, he arranged a job transfer and moved not just to her town, but straight into her house. Rewinding a bit to before his move there were already red flags. On his first visit, he had her install a tracking app to follow his flight. Later, he used it to monitor her every move. She told me how he scolded her for staying out late with friends on a Friday night. Then, the following evening Saturday , he suddenly announced it was his turn to go out despite never mentioning any weekend plans before. That night, he ignored her calls and texts completely. It was only when she messaged something like enjoy your evening out i.e., showing she wasn t bothered by his punishment that he suddenly started talking again. Turns out, he hadn t even gone out he just wanted to punish her.That was just one example among several red flags. I could have sucked it up and ignored those for her sake if she wanted me to had it not been for the one red flag that directly affected me. For context I m gay. Not bi, not on a spectrum just gay. A few months before he moved in, my friend casually mentioned his homophobic views. He was involved with the Freemasons his version was supposedly just prayer gatherings . Another friend told her they were devil worshippers, so she asked him to quit.His response? If he left, then they should live according to the Bible which meant she could no longer be friends with me, because the Bible says gay people should be stoned to death. I immediately told her don t ever expect me to be friends with someone who openly wishes me dead. She basically ignored that. Later, once his job transfer and move were already arranged just days before he moved in , she excitedly said she couldn t wait for me to meet him and join them for weekends at her parents beach house something we used to do often . I reminded her of his homophobia and said there would be no weekends away with all of us together.That s when she started making excuses That I misunderstood him That he didn t mean it like that That he hadn t specifically said I should be stoned but gays in general even though he knew full well I m gay That he just said how Father sees it which struck me, because she s never used the word Father in a religious sense before. None of those excuses change the fact that he openly wished me dead perhaps he would not personally end my life whilst it is against the law, but how can I know for sure that he will never get violent with me . I m generally thick skinned, but I don t waste my energy on homophobic idiots. Spending time with him would be deeply uncomfortable and awkward. I don t want to sit across from someone who thinks I deserve to be killed, pretending everything is fine. That s not just unpleasant it s potentially unsafe. So why should I spend my time with someone like that? My friend thinks I m wrong for refusing to meet him. Am I wrong for refusing to meet him?

caption: My friend killed himself yesterday after calling me to say goodbye. I have a really good internet friend who, when we met had been living in the margins and has had a pretty traumatic life. I'm a software manager and I saw he had skills so I got him work throughout the years. More recently his girlfriend passed away, he had been living alone with his four cats he adored and shifted to doing manual labor. His family dynamic had been deteriorating. He called last night to say he was going to kill himself and wanted to thank me for all I had done. I stayed on the line and offered for him to stay with us for a week to at least have a nice time and he could make up his mind after. He was really set on his plans as it had been in motion for a year. He told me how hungry and lonely he was and felt he was satisfied with all he had done and that life had run its course. He said how scared he was and asked me if I thought it would hurt. I was beside myself. The call ended well but I could tell how determined he was. I reached out to a bunch of mutual friends to figure out where he lived, and we called his old employers. Our friend who lived in the same country called the emergency services and they went to the apartment. They later called saying that he killed himself, around an hour after I had spoken to him. I know I did all I could for the guy and I'm proud that I'm sure I helped him have a better life in some way. I'm grateful that he did reach out to tell me how much he appreciated me and that I got closure. If he hadn't I would have wondered my entire life what would have happened to the guy. I'm well supported but I'm most sad that I don't think anyone will celebrate this guy when I think he deserves to be. So this is my weird way to ask for us to give him a moment of thought since my poor friend deserves better than what life gave him. Thank you for reading this to honor him.

caption: Today I saw the man that saved me when I was being raped. When I was 13 years old I was raped behind a church next to the middle school I attended. I remember it like it was yesterday. As I was catching my breath a man came around the corner. He was much much bigger than I was at 13 years old. I was immediately scared and knew something bad was going to happen. He came up to me and said I was the snack he had been looking for. I tired to run, but he grabbed me and pinned me against the wall. I had no chance of escaping him. He was such a big guy. I ll spare you all the details. The assault happened for around 3 minutes. I was exhausted from trying to fight off this man and trying to scream while he was crushing my body with his. caption: I hate my life. I hate my kid. I resent my family. I resent my inlaws. I resent my wife. I hate myself.. I never wanted kids, but was never adamantly against having one. I get married. My wife knows how I feel about kids. When we were engaged my answer was "maybe one, definitely not more." As my friends started having kids, I started leaning heavily against having kids. Some parents had good kids. Some parents had bad kids. Even the easy kids looked like too much work. Queue my wife's sister dying. All of a sudden "family" is SUPER important to my wife. I get that. At this point my answer to kids was still no. My wife bothered me and bothered and bothered me. Eventually I was convinced. The deal was her parents would sell their ranch and come live on our street. I was convinced. I was so dumb. I was told not to worry about all the realities of having a kid and losing my life because grandma and grandpa are down the street and would be all the parents baby ever needed. Since my wife's sister died she was the only hope for grandkids. My wife and her parents worked me over so good. They convinced me. They made good points. My wife's parents were in their 50's and good health they would be here "beyond the baby phase" and "would have enough energy to keep up with a kid". I'm shown enough Disney movies and Kodak moment and am promised that I just have to be a good dad and provider. A 1950's dad if you will one where the mom unfairly does all the hard stuff. All the good and no bad? Cool fine by me. Well here we are, 11 years later. My kid has "ODD" which is pretty much alphabet soup for your kid being an asshole and defiant. Nothing else is wrong with them the diagnosis is literally that they are vindictive and cruel and seek conflict. Not because they can't communicate or are hypsersensitive to stimuli but just because. Guess what? Grandma and grandpa say the kid is "too much". They haven't helped for more than a day a month in almost 7 years. And here I am on reddit on my laptop, tethered to my phone in a parking lot at the park after dark. I came home from work to my son spitting on the neighbors to door knob his reason "get the neighbors sick". Why does he want them sick? His amazon package got delivered to their house in the morning and they waited until evening to give it to him. Well in returning to for telling him not to do that, my son went into the attic and peed all over the one bankers box of memorabilia I have from my parents who both died before I was 20. I left the house and am sitting in my car. I don't know if I'm coming back. And I don't want advice. This isn't "lack of discipline" or "bad parenting". I've read every book. When I left I calmly told my friend that her comments had made me uncomfortable. Instead of understanding where I was coming from, she got defensive, said that was my problem, and started criticizing my boyfriend, saying he was manipulating me and turning me against her. That really surprised me because he hadn t done any of that. These were my own feelings, and I was the one who decided to bring it up. She later kind of apologized, but it felt more like, I m sorry you felt that way, than acknowledging why I had been uncomfortable. She still seemed to think the issue was entirely mine. I don t think she was trying to flirt with my boyfriend, and I don t think my boyfriend did anything wrong. I m just wondering whether I handled this badly or whether it s reasonable to tell a friend when something they said made you uncomfortable.

caption: I ve been mentally decaying in my room for 10 years, living as a hidden burden to my family. I keep a secret collection of tarantulas just to stay sane. Is there any point to this?. Hey Reddit. I m writing this because I honestly don't know where else to turn anymore. I feel completely hollowed out and hopeless. For context, my mental health issues started back when I was in 7th grade schizophrenia at around age 13 . My family never understood it, they just assumed I was throwing a tantrum or "seeking attention." Growing up, my home felt like an authoritarian regime. I was controlled, yelled at, and constantly punished. They would cut off the internet, cut off the electricity, and slowly strip away every ounce of my dignity. Fast forward over a decade later I ve been on heavy psychiatric medication for over 10 years. The meds numb my brain so badly that I m constantly brain fogged, slow, and exhausted to the point where my doctor had to prescribe another medication just to keep me awake during the day. Because of this, I dropped out, I can't work, and I m completely frozen in time. I have officially become a total, absolute burden to my family. My mom pays for all my medications and hands me around 200 a month just for basic survival. We aren't wealthy, and the economy is terrible right now. Every single dollar she spends on me feels like I'm literally leeching the blood out of the people who raised me. My mom buy me food and pay for electricity and water and everything. and My mom is spending her hard earned money buying meds to keep a life afloat which is a life that I can t even find a reason to keep living anymore. Home feels like an endless nightmare. While everyone else my age is moving forward and building futures, I m frozen in the exact same room, watching myself age into a "bigger burden." Whenever I try to open up to my mom about how broken I am on the inside, all I get back is a look of pure annoyance. She basically tells me to "take your meds and shut up," brushing off my agony as just "overthinking." It s so suffocating here that my mom freaks out over a single ant on the kitchen counter. Because I have zero safe space in this house and feel completely isolated, I did something desperate. Without telling anyone, I secretly keep several tarantulas and a Black Widow in my room. including a highly potent venomous desert scorpion Nobody in my house has any idea. If my mom freaks out over an ant, finding out about them would destroy everything. But keeping those few small lives thriving in total secrecy is literally the only tiny sliver of a safe zone I have left. Outside of my house, things aren't any better. I tried so hard to find connection. I joined Discord servers and sacrificed my tiny allowance to buy Steam games for people, just desperate to feel like I belonged somewhere and had real friends. But the second my money ran out, they discarded me like a ghost. I realized all those "friendships" were purely transactional. I m invisible to the outside world, and an annoyance inside my own home. A while ago, I finally broke down during an argument and screamed at my mom "If raising me is such a burden, just let me die already!" I fight an invisible war inside my own head every single day, and I am utterly exhausted. My soul is shattering every second. So I want to ask you guys honestly If the whole point of taking medication is to survive until tomorrow... but my "tomorrow" only exists so I can wake up, be a burden, and leech my mom's money for more meds... who am I even staying alive for? What am I enduring this for? If outside these walls I m just an invisible ghost, and inside this house I m just a controlled burden whose pain is dismissed as "overthinking"... if there is literally no space on this planet for someone sick and useless like me, what is the world trying to tell me? And if trying to be a normal human being takes every ounce of energy until I m suffocating, only to end up growing older as an annoying burden day after day... am I really supposed to keep denying death and suffer in this same hellhole forever? Is there any actual reason to wake up tomorrow? Any advice on how to handle this would mean the world. currently I'm not in danger of ending my own life

I think the job is moving into a situation where it appears as if they want me to negotiate my own day off instead of a day of been given. This is the post I made earlier in the week Drained from care role I would like to get some help and advice please. Many years ago I started worked for a family close to my home. It was similar to a nanny position but wasn't exactly nannying. I was not live in. Within a few months of paying me a wage they claimed they had difficulty paying me and they found something. I am in Europe. They used their child's disability and my living locality to shove a benefit form under my nose half filled already for me to claim a carers benefit as an income instead of a direct payment or wage from them. I wasn't happy with that but I didn't fight back and it did work out well in the end and I was granted the payment. I had an original contract of hours and work. It was mainly Monday to Friday work but sometimes some other overtime would be expected of me. I was led to suspect maybe that would be like a night babysitting here or there. Things have changed much much much more than what I ever signed up to do originally. I can remember one evening where the mother asked me to stay late on the Thursday night for a Christmas party but I already had plans made for that particular Thursday night. She started sulking and pushing back and forcing me to cancel my plans. I also discovered she lied. She said they would be back at 11 pm but it was more like 1 in the morning so much so I had to stay the night because I would be back again in the morning. The next day was Friday and I thought maybe the parents might come home at a reasonable hour by 6pm because we all had a late night the night before but I was wrong and it was 9 pm finishing time. Imagine that Thursday morning til 9pm Friday night with only 5 hours in the bed over night. I work in a country with employment laws and all of that is wrong. I should have walked then but I never did. My job and my work has changed in so many ways since I started. Over the years the role drifted further and further away from what I originally agreed to. What started as a local caring role became something where more and more was expected of me. There was no single conversation where we sat down and renegotiated the arrangement. It just seemed to happen gradually until I found myself doing things I never would have agreed to at the start. The current situation has finally pushed me to the point where I am becoming genuinely distressed. I recently agreed to provide a live in period of care for the family. I accepted this because I believed I would get some recovery time afterwards. In fact, I specifically remember being told previously that I would likely get some time off when the family returned from their holiday. Instead, while they are away, I have now been informed that they want further cover from me next week, including more overnight responsibilities, without any meaningful break in between. I am exhausted. Last night the child did not settle until around midnight and was awake again around 5.30am. I ended up with a migraine and was physically staggering around from lack of sleep. What upsets me most is that there seems to be an assumption that I can simply keep going indefinitely. The family seem to count only the direct hours spent with their child. They do not seem to count the disrupted nights, the responsibility of being in the house, the household tasks, the cleaning, the laundry, the pets, or the fact that I cannot properly switch off. When the child is at school, in respite, or asleep, it is often treated as if I am automatically "off duty", even though there are still responsibilities waiting for me. What is really bothering me is the complete lack of consideration for my need to rest and recover. The family regularly arrange holidays, social events, races, weddings, dinners and nights out. They understandably want respite from caring responsibilities. What I am struggling with is the fact that they seem to recognise their own need for respite while completely overlooking mine. The latest issue is that the mother wants to go to the races on her birthday and has asked for additional cover from me. I know birthdays are important to people, but I am finding it difficult to understand why her birthday plans seem to take priority over my need for a basic day off after weeks of continuous responsibility. The problem is that over many years I have learned that boundaries are not well received. When I have tried to push back in the past, there has often been guilt, pressure, sulking or attempts to persuade me to change my mind. Looking back, I should probably have enforced stronger boundaries years ago, but I didn't. caption: My girlfriend smells and I don't know what to do. We've been together for 5 years, and not once has she really had a hygiene related problem that was significant enough for me to comment on, until just last week. Out of nowhere I got smacked in the face by a horrible, rotten smell when she hugged me. I didn't even think it was her at first, I honestly thought I might have forgotten to wash my hands after using the bathroom or something, so I went and tidied up. Then we went out to get some groceries, and I got a waft of the same smell while shopping...I finally realized that it was coming from her, and I could smell it from about 3 feet away. Could not believe it. Absolutely wrank. I had to tell her. Some of you might say I'm a dick for that, or "how dare you," etc., I dont really care. I'd want someone to tell me if I smelled like something died. I did it in the nicest way that I possibly could and she actually took it well. She showered when we got home, brushed her teeth, etc...yeah, that didn't help. The thing is, this isn't even really hygienic, per say. She showers everyday, has a hygiene routine and everything. It's not external dirtiness, it's literally coming from inside her. When she sweats even just a little bit when we're in bed, or when she gets home from work where she's been up and about all day, I am hit with these offensive wafts that smell like literal diarrhea. I'm not even trying to be mean, the smell is so putrid and repulsive, it literally makes me wince and want to puke. The worst part is, her breath has the same smell even after brushing her teeth. This makes me think it's health related somehow, I don't think I've heard of this being a symptom of anything before, but honestly what else what it would be? Totally random, has never happened even once. I just don't understand. She has smelled like this for almost 2 weeks straight, and honestly the part that worries me most aside from it being health related , is that she doesn't even seem to notice it. I can guarantee with certainty that her coworkers and friends certainly do. Just sucks, I am finding myself avoiding being in close proximity to her and I don't want to make her feel bad. What the fuck do I do? Anyone know why she smells? Does she need to see a doctor? FIRST UPDATE A minor one, but since so many people are interested, I'll gladly honor that in light of all of your help. I broke it to her and put the pressure on, she took it pretty well. She has an appointment with a PCP this coming Monday, and we are getting her scheduled with a dentist the same week. Wish us luck! SECOND UPDATE She had her appointment with the PCP this morning, and unfortunately no big revelations so far. We're still in the dark about what's going on. Some labs were conducted including a blood panel and a PAP, so there is a chance that the results may be enlightening. Until then, next up is the dentist and I have a feeling this is where we may finally get some answers. Will update again post appointment. THIRD UPDATE I do have a few revelations to share, and one of them actually pertains to me! Just not in the way many people in this thread suggested. 1st thing It turns out that one of the antibiotics I am taking amplifies my sense of smell to bloodhound levels. I am smelling all things x100 from distance, including my girlfriend. Keep in mind that it is not altered, but amplified. caption: I rushed, and I regret it an alumnus' perspective. Hey everybody. I'm 23M, and I graduated last year. I was in a frat, and I was very popular. I had leadership positions within Greek life and the house I was in specifically. My resume found great success, but I'm hear to say that despite what your parents have said about their greek life experiences, despite what those energetic friends of yours are saying about greek life, despite what you see on barstool sports, and despite my opening couple of sentences please, please, please don't rush your freshman year if you can help it at all . Honestly, whatever floats your boat, but if you're not the type to drink all the time, give zero shits about classes and, by proxy, your future , or generally not care greatly about yourself and your life please reconsider rushing, period. I rushed because my dad pushed me to do so. He was in a frat, and is obsessed with his time in college, even now, over 40 years later. I never understood the draw, but I figured that if my literal father figure had such positive experiences, it couldn't hurt me either. It did. It did badly, and in unseen ways. I didn't take the time to learn myself first, and spend some uncomfortable time alone in college, getting to know myself and my interests. Instead, I jumped headfirst into a centuries old culture of abuse and strict hierarchy both formally and socially , thinking it would be different because my frat said that they were 'not like the rest', and to their credit, for a bit they weren't. Then the school year started. To give you a quick rundown For the first semester, I effectively had another full time class the frat. Yes, they assigned homework, and we had mandatory meetings each week, with drills after each meeting to see what we knew. I say drills and laugh, because here's what it actually was all of us new members, not yet initiated mind you on our feet in the dark basement in front of a fireplace, screaming at the top of our lungs the information we were expected to know. Our frat wasn't as abusive as others on campus, but if you got something wrong, you stood in front of the fire, and for each time thereafter you got something wrong, you took a step closer to the fire. One guy's pants started smoking, just from having to stand in front of the flames which were constantly made larger . This was once a week, for the entire first semester of college oh, and you're in a suit for this too. You'll see the pledges on campus khakis, white shirt, blue jacket, red tie, and complete exhaustion in their eyes . After initiation, nothing changes. You're not special, and in fact, people are less interested in you, because you're not someone who can be bullied as easily anymore. However, bullying and harassment are still rampant. Get ready to keep your porcupine quills up the whole time you're there, because if there's one thing that a group of toxic, insecure people are always looking for, it's the next downward punching bag. Oh, but if you defend the person getting bullied, you get sucked into the fold, too. I mentioned I was popular I used this 'soft power' to step in and defend as many people as I could, but something else about frats if the bullying gets exposed, they just get better at hiding it. It's an absolutely brutal and immature loop that honestly only gets more complicated as the years of college go on. It's not a game you can win unless you physically throw down which everyone wants to do already or leave. There is no academic support, there is no alumni network, there are no job perks after college. I don't give a shit what the promo stuff they give you says. Those are for the guys who rush at frats where their daddies are big contributors, and almost only for those guys. If you find something, it's blind luck. Also, even if there are alumni looking to hire ask yourself if they're really people you want to work for and with. Are they actually different from the people you so despise now, or are they just older versions of those guys? I'll tell you right now, 9 10 times it's the latter . The houses say they have study hours and study times try getting work done. I dare you. For several months, I literally spent more hours in the library on campus than I did almost anywhere else. Maybe that's typical. But is it such a crime to want to work peacefully at the place you reside? The alumni network consisted of whoever the fuck showed up on gamedays, and they were always piss hammered anyways, so it didn't matter what you said to them. They weren't going to remember you. The culture is drinking. That's it. That's literally it. I want to elaborate, but doing so would only dilute this point. I abstained from drinking for the sake of self improvement after my first semester freshman year, and found myself almost immediately devoid of any relatable group of people. It was really weird, actually. People treated me like I had a problem because I didn't drink like a fish. Now, these are the biggest four. I could go on for ages, but that's to be saved for my therapist. I'll also say that, yes. I chose to do this. Yes, I chose to pay 900 a semester and 500 a month for rent, just to be miserable. Yes, I could have gotten out! But then do what? I'd have to find housing and the money to pay for it, for one while paying for the frat, because you're locked into year long lease contracts at the house if you want to or can live there. How did it hurt me in unseen ways, you ask? It's a hard one to articulate, but it definitely has to do with not feeling fit in at all for four years without feeling like there was any out, while having a full courseload, while working weekends and any spare time at all to support yourself I had to pay dues and most of rent myself , so no time to socialize in the only way the only people around you seem to know how. I've spent this past year debriefing reeling trying to process my college experience and figure out who the fuck I actually am because I didn't get that chance or, rather, give myself that chance in college. Now, I want to be very clear. It's very easy for the older ones of us to look back at this life and be like 'well, duh. of course a frat is going to be that way.' how do you know that? how did you know that? how would those who don't or didn't have positive role models, or any at all, know that, before going to college? And before I hear 'just look it up online', politics has shown us that that just doesn't fucking work. If you've made it this far, thanks for the read. If you're on your way to college, think twice about rushing. If you've already rushed, don't beat yourself up, but still do some thinking about where you are, who you are, where you want to go, and who you want to be, and if the organization you've joined will actually help you get there, or only create more swamp to trudge through in pursuit of your goals. edit " if the bullying gets exposed, they just get better at hiding it. " this is why frat rituals the frat itself is are so secretive. You don't talk publicly about things you're embarassed to be doing. edit 2 " Yes, I chose to pay 900 a semester and 500 a month for rent, just to be miserable." This was the cheapest option on my campus at the time. There were scant financial support opportunities on my campus for those who were financially insecure. I ask for your consideration what would they do? EDIT 3 AND THIS ONE IS IMPORTANT I forgot to talk about the rampant R A M P A N T homophobia in Greek Life. Like it's actually insane. Speaking for frats specifically here, everyone has such an inflated ego that everyone thinks that everyone is hitting on them including the dudes and because these are the ultra dude bro type, no homo was the name of the game. To the Nth power. We had a couple of openly gay guys in the house when I first got there, which was cool. Everyone was too afraid to talk to them because they were too afraid of being perceived as gay. They all dropped in mass when they realized how much the guys in the house fucking hated gay people. This was because those guys stopped hiding it, and the rest of the house didn't care enough to stand up for them I was only one person, mind you, in the face of 100 . I really can't say that their safety was ensured, but thank God they never stayed at the house for long enough to find out. If you're unsure as to your sexuality, there's nothing wrong with that just please be really, really careful around frats. With centuries old institutions comes centuries old customs...and opinions.

caption: I'm surrounded by people, but no one is truly on my team. I feel like the last person on Earth.. I m 31 now. Growing up, I was an only child. My mom moved abroad for work when I was 5, and my dad was almost never home. Before she left, we lived with my grandfather in a small three room apartment. He used to physically abuse my mom, and my dad would constantly get into screaming matches with him. He never hit me, but maybe that was only because my mom rarely left me alone with him and when she did, she locked me in my room for safety. After she left, I was moved to live with my maternal grandmother, who was a deeply conservative, strict Christian. My childhood with her was marked by a lot of physical abuse. We moved to the countryside, where the greatest luxury of the 21st century was having proper sewage. My days consisted of absolute solitude, working in the garden, and taking care of the animals and the household. I had no friends everyone avoided me i think because i was a bit different, introvertes kinda in my own world I coped by reading books, building radios, and obsessing over all things nerdy. I lived like this until I was 18. The moment I could, I left. I moved to another country for university and finally started a life of my own. My parents would call me occasionally, but it almost always turned into uncomfortable, bitter arguments. Later, I met my boyfriend, whom I love endlessly. His family is welcoming, though I really only connect with his mom. So why am I writing this? Throughout my entire life, I have grown accustomed to loneliness. It became like a deep pit in the ground that I knew I could never climb out of so instead of fighting it, I decorated it like a living room and learned how to live in it. But sometimes, there are days like today where it hits me harder than usual there is not a single person on this planet who is 100 in my corner. My parents moved away, and we have a very cold, formal relationship. I have no contact with the grandmother who raised me due to family feuds. My boyfriend s family will never truly be my family whenever I try to open up to them, they just wave it off and tell me I "overthink things too much." And as fantastic and supportive as my boyfriend is, I can't always share everything with him especially when the thing bothering me involves his own family. Nobody is fully on my team. I am completely surrounded by people, yet I feel like the only person left on the planet. I don't know if it's a result of my conservative upbringing, but I am a spiritual person. I believe in God not necessarily organized religion or the church, just a higher power. When I was a little girl, I used to talk to Him all the time. I d tell Him about my day, what I experienced, what I was thinking about... simply because I had no one else to talk to. That habit stuck with me. I talk to Him less often now, but today I completely broke down in the shower. A thought suddenly crossed my mind "If God doesn't exist, I am completely fucked." And right there, under the water, I just started laughing through my tears at the twisted, sick humor of my life.

caption: Loneliness isn t fixed by hobbies or just go out advice. Stop it.. I keep hearing the same advice given to lonely people just pick up a hobby, go meet new people, stop being lazy. I did all that this year. Didn't work. Why? Because that style of message misses the main issue. Hobbies don t replace human connection. Simple. They can keep you busy, but they don t provide meaningful interaction. You can spend all day painting, running, or learning the ukulele and still feel alone because no one really sees you. Saying make new friends assumes everyone has the same opportunities, which is not true. Social anxiety, personal circumstances lost my fianc two years ago , and technology replacing deep connections with superficial ones, these problems can t be fixed by simply saying go to a meetup. Trust me, I've been there. Even when you try, man.. they are all shallow connections, at best. Those won't satisfy the need for real intimacy! No idea why people keep giving away that advice! Technology itself adds to the problem. I am a software developer, so I know a thing or two about this as well. We hear the whole "we re more connected than ever", which is BS. Pure and simple BS. Most online interactions are either performative or transactional. Likes, direct messages, and comments don t replace the need for presence, empathy, or shared experiences. So before anyone suggests just be proactive or stop moping, let s recognize this loneliness is structural, not a personal flaw. It s not about laziness or a lack of hobbies. Saying it can be fixed with simple activities is really just telling people to distract themselves until life ends. That s not advice. It s avoidance. Joining a club doesn t always help either. A lot of people there are messed up too, and it shows. Sometimes things get dark. Even if it s a board game club, it doesn t mean you ll find healthy or real connections. It s no replacement for genuine relationships. First thing therapists do with people who is not "really well", and I'm talking about people who perhaps should get help some other way, is telling them to join a club. So you go to a tabletop club or some other club, idk, language exchange group or whatever, and you'll find people who is okay, but some are freaky as hell. So it becomes toxic really soon and you end up not wanting to be there anymore. Worse than square one is square 10. To truly tackle loneliness, we need societal solutions better community structures, spaces for real human interaction, and an understanding that technology can isolate us instead of connecting us. How we get there, I've no damn clue. All I know is it's been more than a week and, aside from work, no one gives me a call. It s Saturday night. If I were to drop dead right now, it might not be until Thursday or Friday, maybe even next Saturday before anyone tried to get through the door to see what stinks. No one would have checked on me. No family, so most likely would be a quick cremation by the city. I'm 40 years old. It is already time for me to face the fact that it is over. At 40, no friends, no family, that's it. So, what can we do?

caption: Spiraling, Surviving, and Trying to Breathe Hi. It’s Tina. And yes—before anyone asks—I know I should be sleeping right now. Like, a normal person should be asleep, phone face-down, body heavy with that “everything is fine” feeling. But no. Here I am at 9:20 PM, still wired. Still replaying the day like it’s a highlight reel of bad decisions, bad timing, and bad luck—except the “highlights” are mostly me getting grilled at work, feeling like I need to defend my existence, and then breaking down in tears in my own driveway like I just got dumped by a toaster. Usually, I can come on here, make a joke, throw in a little sarcasm, tell you how somebody irritated my soul before 9:00 in the morning, and somehow turn whatever mess I’m dealing with into something we can all laugh about. But today? Baby, the humor department is understaffed. The sarcasm manager called out. My last nerve submitted a two-week notice without consulting me. Emotionally, I feel like I have been dragged behind a moving vehicle all day while somebody periodically leaned out the window to ask, “But have you thought about what you did?” YES. I HAVE THOUGHT ABOUT WHAT I DID. THANK YOU. At this point, I have thought about it in regular font, bold font, italics, Times New Roman, Arial, and probably Wingdings. Let me explain (as much as I legally can) so I can get this out of my head before I swallow so much stress it turns into a scientific anomaly in my bloodstream. I got into a massive problem at work today. The kind of problem I literally cannot talk about in detail because there is an investigation pending and everything is in limbo. I could say one wrong thing and accidentally create a whole new problem on top of the original one. And honestly? I’ve already done enough damage for one lifetime. I did something stupid. Not an “Oops, I forgot my lunch in the refrigerator” mistake. Not an “I sent the email without the attachment” mistake. This was the kind of mistake where I literally had the right information, my intuition told me better, and I still chose to ignore it and do it anyway. Which is, in my opinion, the absolute worst kind of stupid. There is no dramatic villain I can blame. I cannot blame Mercury retrograde, the economy, or daylight saving time. I screwed up. So now, I am stuck in this agonizing holding pattern. I was told I have to wait 3 to 4 weeks to find out if I get to keep my job or if I’m getting fired. Do you know how long three or four weeks feels when somebody is holding your livelihood over a trap door? That is not three to four weeks. That is approximately 743 emotional years. Three to four weeks is enough time to: Reorganize your entire house. Overthink one conversation approximately 4,000 times. Search “what happens if you lose your job?” at two in the morning. Imagine every possible outcome, including the ones that make absolutely zero sense. Every time my phone rings, I’m going to jump. Every time an email pops up, my stomach is going to fall into my shoes. Please communicate with me exclusively through carrier pigeon until further notice. To make matters worse, my morning started with a grueling meeting involving the big wigs from regional. I was attacked—emotionally attacked—and grilled from left to right. It wasn’t one question. It was a waterfall of “explain this, justify that, what were you thinking?” And the part that makes me furious is that I sat there, owning my truth and taking full accountability for my monumental screw-up, and yet, it was heavily insinuated that I was lying. There is nothing quite as maddening as telling the complete truth about a mistake you’re already kicking yourself for, only to have a room full of people look at you like you’re spinning a fairy tale. I wasn’t trying to dodge accountability. I was owning my truth. But owning your truth in a room like that doesn’t feel empowering; it feels like you’re being asked to prove your innocence with no room for your humanity. Now, my husband and I both work in healthcare. Usually, this is a blessing. We get the jargon, we understand the burnout. He always has my back, and I know he will always defend me. But this particular situation? Because of the healthcare overlap, he knows enough to ask questions. So, instead of coming home, removing my bra and my emotional responsibilities, and letting my nervous system unclench with a glass of wine, I walked straight out of Interview Room A at work and into Interview Room B at home. My husband essentially became the Regional Director, HR, Legal Counsel, FBI Special Agent, and Judge Judy all at the same time. Sir. Please clock out. I am begging you. He kept questioning me: Why did you do this? What happened here? What were you thinking? Didn’t you know? I know he is scared too. If I lose my job, that affects our household, our finances, and our plans. But there comes a point where questioning stops being productive and starts feeling like punishment. I spent hours defending myself against regional managers, only to clock out, walk through my front door, and get cross-examined by my own spouse until 9:20 at night. I kept thinking: How many different ways can you ask me the same question before one of us starts speaking Latin? Nobody is more aware of the mistake than the person whose entire career is currently hanging in uncertainty because of it. I don’t need somebody standing beside me yelling, “THE HOUSE IS ON FIRE!” Baby, I am inside the house. I see the flames. Sometimes, when a person is already drowning, you don’t stand on the dock explaining all the swimming techniques they should have used before they fell in. First, you help them breathe. If I’m being completely honest, the reason this work drama and the marital bickering feel so heavy is because my emotional tank has been running on empty for a very long time. What people don’t always see is that the thing that finally makes you break down isn’t actually the biggest thing happening in your life. It’s just the final thing. Because while all of this work chaos is happening, I am carrying a grief that feels impossible to put into words. I am navigating the silent, brutal trenches of IVF. I am dealing with the constant, devastating heartbreak of losing a child and having transfers not fully go through time and time again. There is a specific type of exhaustion that comes with wanting a child so desperately, and feeling like your own body keeps making you audition for motherhood without ever giving you the role. Infertility has a way of turning time into a measuring device: You measure days. You measure hormones and follicles. You measure hope. You measure loss. I am doing every single thing right. I’m following every protocol, trying everything humanly possible, looking at pregnancy tests under bathroom lights like I’m conducting forensic analysis—and yet, it’s just not happening for me. It is a profound, unique kind of pain to realize that despite how hard you fight, you might just have to accept the fate that no matter how many IVF treatments you endure, you may never be able to carry a child. So when you are carrying that kind of physical, mental, and emotional trauma, a mistake at work doesn’t just feel like a bump in the road. It feels like the entire road is collapsing underneath you. My brain decided to write the worst possible ending to every storyline simultaneously today: Job? Gone. IVF? Never happening. Marriage? Everybody irritated. Mental health? Somewhere underneath the driver’s seat of my car. Eventually, my emotional system said: Absolutely not. We are closed. Please come back during normal business hours. I broke down. I sat in my car in the driveway and cried. And I don’t mean cute, single-tear movie crying. I mean UGLY crying. Shoulders shaking, can’t catch your breath, mascara applying for asylum, snot making an unexpected guest appearance. The type of cry where if somebody knocked on the window, you would seriously consider relocating to another state rather than making eye contact. I cried about work. I cried because I was scared. I cried because I was ashamed of my stupid decision. I cried because my husband kept questioning me when I desperately just needed him to hug me. I cried because every unsuccessful IVF attempt leaves another tiny crack in me that I don’t know how to repair. I cried because I am so tired of being strong. And after crying in my car, I pulled myself together just enough to walk upstairs… and broke down all over again. Apparently, tonight’s program was a double feature. I don’t have a motivational ending for you. I don’t have a beautiful quote about everything happening for a reason. Sometimes things happen because you made a mistake, and sometimes life is just unfair. Today, three completely separate emotional disasters decided to RSVP to the same Tuesday without an invitation. But I am trying to remind myself that one horrible day does not get to decide the rest of my life. One mistake doesn’t erase every good thing I have done professionally. One investigation doesn’t dictate the final verdict. One unsuccessful IVF journey doesn’t tell me with certainty what my future holds. And one argument with my husband doesn’t erase the fact that we love each other deeply. I am going to try to give myself some grace tonight. Not the Instagram version where you light a candle and your problems respectfully disappear. The ugly version. The version where I admit: I screwed up, I am terrified, I don’t have control, and I am still deserving of rest. You do not have to earn rest by having a perfect life. You do not have to earn compassion by never making mistakes. So tonight, I’m emotionally clocking out. The investigation will be there tomorrow. My fears will be waiting. IVF will still be part of my story. But tonight, I need somebody to tell the committee inside my head that today’s proceedings have officially adjourned. If you are reading this and you’ve ever had one of those days where everything falls apart in layers—work stress, relationship stress, fertility stress, grief—you are not alone. You are not weak for breaking down. Sometimes your body doesn’t break because you can’t handle it; it breaks because you handled it for far longer than you should have. I’m Tina. I’m scared. I’m exhausted. But I’m still here. Now I’m going to do the one thing I should’ve done hours ago. I’m going to try to breathe like I’m not carrying the whole world in my chest. caption: How MS Edge’s Immersive Reader Helps Me Slow Down We all probably know the drill of a typical workday: back-to-back meetings, side conversations in team chats about some other topics, drafting & scanning emails, creating Jira issues, and juggling multiple project threads. The sheer volume of information coming in such a short time can be challenging. Normally, this isn’t an issue for me. But sometimes I find myself struggling to read long texts in the middle of these high-intensity stretches. Not because I lack the time, but because my mind is already racing ahead to the next thing. I can’t seem to slow it down. This is annoying and, to be honest, a little frightening , because I realise that my mind is in a very short-cycle mode – clear evidence that I’m under stress . Over time, I’ve found a simple trick that helps: Microsoft Edge’s Immersive Reader mode. I don’t just use it to declutter the according web page. I let the browser read the text out loud to me. Yes, that’s right! I hit the play button, lean back, and keep my hands off the mouse and keyboard to avoid getting distracted by other tabs or windows. It forces me to slow down and listen instead of skimming the whole page. It eliminates the temptation to jump between paragraphs or skim entire sections. It enforces a slower pace that I have to accept. At first, it’s a bit of a struggle – but I’ve come to realize: it helps me to calm down a bit. If you ever feel overwhelmed by the sheer speed of work, maybe give it a try. The film does feature a few very beautiful shots, particularly of bodily fluids and the interior of bodies. Yes, unfortunately it’s reminiscent of The Substance (2024) , which I hated. The film’s main flaw is that it’s a mix of Coralie Fargeat’s film and Grave (2016) , which I didn’t like at all either. That’s saying something! Two female directors I can’t stand. As for Grave , it’s the carnal aspect centred on food that puts me off. The film might have been more successful if it had been cut by a good half an hour. As it stands, it’s rather repetitive and very boring. The storyline centred on the heroine’s family, which is very interesting, would have deserved more screen time. Two parents doing their best, but their best isn’t very high. Between the father, who struggles to do anything, and the mother, who goes overboard. In fact, she reminded me of my own worries. Those mothers who are always wanting to tidy and clean their children’s bedrooms without realising that they’re intruding on a private world they can’t possibly understand. We throw things away and clean up without realising that this mess might have had its own significance, symbolic or otherwise. We know that stories about weight will attract an audience, just as we know it’s just as easy to have a hit with a film about money. Like when people come into a fortune and decide to keep it to themselves without telling anyone else. So it’s the same with stories where someone finds a miracle solution for losing weight. These are indeed constant, permanent and eternal problems for people in our society. What a sad world! This film is, of course, rather despicable. The subject matter is repulsive, especially when you discover what’s in the so-called miracle pills. The atmosphere is as grim as you could wish for. The lead actress is truly unsettling, which does, however, demonstrate a certain talent. But there comes a point where it all gets completely ridiculous, and from that moment on, I gradually lost interest. It hadn’t really managed to hold my attention right from the start. At least this film doesn’t really make you fancy a bite to eat. That’s the cool thing about it if you’re watching it with the aim of losing a few kilos! Saccharine offers nothing particularly meaty or substantial to sink your teeth into. Forrest Gump says “Life is like a box of chocolates”, but not quite so for obese people. It’s glaringly obvious that this film lacks subtlety. We can add a third film that I hated to the list of what this film reminded me of. Indeed, Antiviral (2012) by Cronenberg Jr, Brandon, can round off my list of a quartet of despicable films to avoid. Except for the most twisted among us, of course. Fans of the macabre, gore and grim, sickening atmospheres can rush headlong into these films without hesitation. If the plot invokes the miracle weight-loss pill, the filmmaker would do well to find the formula for a successful pace, surprise and dramatic tension – essential ingredients for concocting genuine intellectual satisfaction. Natalie Erika James, an American, Australian and Japanese director, screenwriter and producer, is no doubt trying to show that she can shock and disgust even more than men, whilst thinking she’s doing a better job. But with slow service and bland food, it’s a definite NO! The trio of leading actresses do a fine job. Midori Francis , Madeleine Madden , and Danielle Macdonald are quite good, but Danielle Macdonald is excellent. I would have loved to see more of her in this film. All her scenes are the best in my opinion. Somewhere between body horror and a ghost film, Saccharine , Natalie Erika James’s third feature film, suffers from a thematic overload, tackling themes such as the cult of thinness, eating disorders and female desire. The sweetness is there, as are the intentions, but it doesn’t quite hit the spot. ⭐ Rating: 1 out of 5. australia bodyHorror bodyImage gore horror saccharine2026 weightLoss

caption: When Bullies Punch Down, I Punch Back (and Why I’m Done Being Quiet) I hate bullies. I hate them with a passion. Not in a casual, eye-roll way. I mean a deep, lived-in dislike that comes from decades of being on the receiving end of their cruelty. I was born with a lazy eye, clinically known as strabismus. It is part of my body. It is part of my face. It is something I did not choose and cannot control. And for as long as I can remember, it has been an open invitation for strangers, classmates, and now internet randos to say something slick, “funny,” or outright cruel. If you have ever been bullied for your appearance, your body, your condition, your disability, your neurodivergence, your accent, or simply for existing a little outside the norm, you already know this story. It starts young. It hurts deeply. And at first, it makes you cry. I cried. A lot. But at some point, crying stopped working. The moment anger replaced shame There was a turning point in my childhood where sadness hardened into anger. Not the kind of anger that destroys you from the inside, but the kind that wakes you up. The kind that says, “No. I am not the problem here.” Bullies taught me several things, whether they meant to or not. They taught me that bullies are scared human beings. They taught me that bullies suffer deeply. They taught me that bullies will grab onto anything they perceive as smaller, different, or vulnerable so they can punch down and feel powerful for five fleeting seconds. I am not offering some groundbreaking psychological insight here. We have all heard it before. Hurt people hurt people. But here is where I draw the line. I refuse to be hurt by hurt people. Once I understood how deeply insecure bullies actually are, something shifted in me. I stopped internalizing their words. I stopped assuming they were right. And I started talking back. Why I stopped being polite about my pain When someone is bold enough to comment on my body, my eye, or my condition, something I cannot change, then they have forfeited my politeness. That realization is how I survived that part of my childhood. I matched their energy. I named their behavior. I made it clear I was not ashamed. Was it always graceful? No. Was it effective? Absolutely. Because bullies rely on silence. They rely on you shrinking. They rely on shame doing their work for them. When you speak up, when you push back, when you show them that their words do not own you, their power evaporates. They are suddenly exposed for what they are: insecure people flailing for control. Screenshot 1 Online bullies are not different. They are louder. Fast forward to adulthood, and the setting has changed, but the behavior has not. The playground is now a comment section. The whispers are now public replies. The cruelty is now dressed up as “jokes.” Recently, I received a comment on one of my videos that leaned on an old, lazy, ableist joke about my eye. The kind of joke that bullies think is clever because they have heard it echoed a thousand times before. I responded. Not because I needed validation. Not because I was hurt. But because I refuse to be silent. Online or offline, I will call out nasty behavior when I see it. I will point to it directly and say, “This is what you are doing, and it is not cute.” This blog post is part of that same refusal. Where my confidence really came from I need to say this clearly: I did not get here alone. I was fortunate. Deeply fortunate. My grandmother raised me to know there was nothing wrong with me. She did not minimize my pain, but she never let me believe the cruelty I faced was deserved. She taught me that the problem was never my face, my eye, or my existence. The problem was always the people who felt entitled to comment on it. That foundation matters. Because when you grow up being told you are whole, you are far less likely to believe people who try to tear you apart. Thanks to her, I learned how to stand up for myself. I learned how to take up space. I learned how to speak without apologizing for my body. Screenshot The truth bullies do not want you to see Here is the part that makes bullies uncomfortable. The joke is never really about you. The joke is about their emptiness. People who know and love themselves do not need to mock someone else’s body to feel joy. People who are secure do not punch down. People who are at peace do not need to humiliate others for entertainment. Ableist jokes are not humor. They are confessions. They confess fear. They confess self-loathing. They confess a desperate need to feel above someone, anyone, for a brief moment. That is why I can say, without hesitation, that the joke is on him. I know myself. I love myself. And I do not need to tear someone else apart to feel worthy. Bullies cannot say the same. If you are being bullied, read this slowly If you are reading this and you are being bullied right now, I want you to hear this clearly. The problem is not you existing. The problem is not your body. The problem is not your condition. The problem is not your disability. The problem is not your difference. The problem is the bully who cannot stand to see you exist because your existence reminds them of the hatred they carry toward themselves. You do not owe anyone silence. You do not owe anyone softness. You do not owe anyone understanding at the expense of your dignity. Whether you choose to clap back, block, educate, or walk away, the choice is yours. Power looks different for everyone. What matters is that you do not internalize their cruelty as truth. You are not too much. You are not broken. You are not wrong for taking up space. And if no one has told you this lately, let me say it plainly. You deserve to exist loudly, confidently, and unapologetically. Even when bullies wish you would disappear.
